def is_terminal(self) -> bool:
        """Check if the console is writing to a terminal.

        Returns:
            bool: True if the console writing to a device capable of
                understanding escape sequences, otherwise False.
        """
        # If dev has explicitly set this value, return it
        if self._force_terminal is not None:
            return self._force_terminal

        # Fudge for Idle
        if hasattr(sys.stdin, "__module__") and sys.stdin.__module__.startswith(
            "idlelib"
        ):
            # Return False for Idle which claims to be a tty but can't handle ansi codes
            return False

        if self.is_jupyter:
            # return False for Jupyter, which may have FORCE_COLOR set
            return False

        environ = self._environ

        tty_compatible = environ.get("TTY_COMPATIBLE", "")
        # 0 indicates device is not tty compatible
        if tty_compatible == "0":
            return False
        # 1 indicates device is tty compatible
        if tty_compatible == "1":
            return True

        # https://force-color.org/
        force_color = environ.get("FORCE_COLOR")
        if force_color is not None:
            return force_color != ""

        # Any other value defaults to auto detect
        isatty: Optional[Callable[[], bool]] = getattr(self.file, "isatty", None)
        try:
            return False if isatty is None else isatty()
        except ValueError:
            # in some situation (at the end of a pytest run for example) isatty() can raise
            # ValueError: I/O operation on closed file
            # return False because we aren't in a terminal anymore
            return False

        include_new_lines: bool = True,

        Args:

                generated from console.render.

            pad (bool): Enable padding of lines that are less than `length`.

            Iterable[List[Segment]]: An iterable of lines of segments.

        Args:

            indent (Union[None, int, str], optional): Number of characters to indent by. Defaults to 2.
            highlight (bool, optional): Enable highlighting. Defaults to True.

        json = dumps(
            data,
            indent=indent,
            skipkeys=skip_keys,
            ensure_ascii=ensure_ascii,
            check_circular=check_circular,
            allow_nan=allow_nan,
            default=default,

    overflow: Optional["OverflowMethod"] = None,
) -> "ConsoleRenderable":
    """Render python variables in a given scope.

    Args:
        scope (Mapping): A mapping containing variable names and values.
        title (str, optional): Optional title. Defaults to None.
        sort_keys (bool, optional): Enable sorting of items. Defaults to True.
        indent_guides (bool, optional): Enable indentation guides. Defaults to False.
        max_length (int, optional): Maximum length of containers before abbreviating, or None for no abbreviation.

    Returns:
        ConsoleRenderable: A renderable object.

    highlighter = ReprHighlighter()
    items_table = Table.grid(padding=(0, 1), expand=False)
    items_table.add_column(justify="right")

    def sort_items(item: Tuple[str, Any]) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
        """Sort special variables first, then alphabetically."""
        key, _ = item
        return (not key.startswith("__"), key.lower())

    items = sorted(scope.items(), key=sort_items) if sort_keys else scope.items()
    for key, value in items:
        key_text = Text.assemble(
            (key, "scope.key.special" if key.startswith("__") else "scope.key"),
            (" =", "scope.equals"),
        )
        items_table.add_row(
            key_text,
            Pretty(
                value,
                highlighter=highlighter,
                indent_guides=indent_guides,
                max_length=max_length,
                max_string=max_string,
                max_depth=max_depth,
                overflow=overflow,
            ),
        )
    return Panel.fit(
        items_table,
        title=title,
        border_style="scope.border",
        padding=(0, 1),
    )

        check_circular: bool = True,

        sort_keys: bool = False,

        Args:
            data (Any): An object that may be encoded in to JSON
            indent (Union[None, int, str], optional): Number of characters to indent by. Defaults to 2.
            highlight (bool, optional): Enable highlighting. Defaults to True.
            default (Callable, optional): Optional callable which will be called for objects that cannot be serialized. Defaults to None.
            skip_keys (bool, optional): Skip keys not of a basic type. Defaults to False.

            check_circular (bool, optional): Check for circular references. Defaults to True.
            allow_nan (bool, optional): Allow NaN and Infinity values. Defaults to True.

        Returns:
            JSON: New JSON object from the given data.

        json = dumps(
            data,
            indent=indent,
            skipkeys=skip_keys,
            ensure_ascii=ensure_ascii,
            check_circular=check_circular,
            allow_nan=allow_nan,
            default=default,
            sort_keys=sort_keys,
        )

            (0, False, 0),

            *((span.end, True, index) for index, span in enumerated_spans),

def render(self, console: "Console", end: str = "") -> Iterable["Segment"]:
        """Render the text as Segments.

        Args:
            console (Console): Console instance.
            end (Optional[str], optional): Optional end character.

        Returns:
            Iterable[Segment]: Result of render that may be written to the console.
        """
        _Segment = Segment
        text = self.plain
        if not self._spans:
            yield Segment(text)
            if end:
                yield _Segment(end)
            return
        get_style = partial(console.get_style, default=Style.null())

        enumerated_spans = list(enumerate(self._spans, 1))
        style_map = {index: get_style(span.style) for index, span in enumerated_spans}
        style_map[0] = get_style(self.style)

        spans = [
            (0, False, 0),
            *((span.start, False, index) for index, span in enumerated_spans),
            *((span.end, True, index) for index, span in enumerated_spans),
            (len(text), True, 0),
        ]

        stack_pop = stack.remove

        combine = Style.combine

        def get_current_style() -> Style:
            """Construct current style from stack."""
            styles = tuple(style_map[_style_id] for _style_id in sorted(stack))
            cached_style = style_cache_get(styles)
            if cached_style is not None:
                return cached_style
            current_style = combine(styles)
            style_cache[styles] = current_style
            return current_style

            if leaving:
                stack_pop(style_id)
            else:
                stack_append(style_id)

                yield _Segment(text[offset:next_offset], get_current_style())

        check_circular: bool = True,

        sort_keys: bool = False,

        Args:
            data (Any): An object that may be encoded in to JSON
            indent (Union[None, int, str], optional): Number of characters to indent by. Defaults to 2.
            highlight (bool, optional): Enable highlighting. Defaults to True.
            default (Callable, optional): Optional callable which will be called for objects that cannot be serialized. Defaults to None.
            skip_keys (bool, optional): Skip keys not of a basic type. Defaults to False.

            check_circular (bool, optional): Check for circular references. Defaults to True.
            allow_nan (bool, optional): Allow NaN and Infinity values. Defaults to True.

        Returns:
            JSON: New JSON object from the given data.

        json = dumps(
            data,
            indent=indent,
            skipkeys=skip_keys,
            ensure_ascii=ensure_ascii,
            check_circular=check_circular,
            allow_nan=allow_nan,
            default=default,
            sort_keys=sort_keys,
        )

        """Render the sub_layouts.
